newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares inch ahead, rail freight rates raised.
newsitem.headline: India shares inch ahead, rail freight rates raised.

text.p: ** (1315 GMT) - Indian shares end almost unchanged
** Bombay's top index finishes 8.14 points, or 0.24 pct, up
at 3,364.97, off 3,367.38-intra-day high
** Railway budget announced on Wednesday has little impact
on stock prices, already discounted, say dealers
** Government announces 12 percent hike in freight charges
for most commodities
** National Stock Exchange index rises 2.75 points, 0.28
percent, to 968.85
** Delhi share index edges 1.24 pts to 728.26, Calcutta
1.76 pts to 442.71, Madras falls 9.47 pts to 3,343.20
Indian stocks at major bourses drifted on Wednesday, with the announcement of the railway budget having little impact on prices, dealers said.
The government plans to raise freight rates by 12 percent for all commodities, barring essentials, and for all distances, Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan announced in his 1997/98 railway budget.
"The market was expecting a hike of 12-15 percent," said chief dealer Ketan Jhaveri at local brokerage Kotak Securities.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top 30-share index ended 8.14 points higher at 3,364.97 in a day of rangebound trade.

The increased freight rates which exclude 15 essential items such as foodgrains and pulses, edible oils, kerosene, sugar, liquefied petroleum gas, fruits and jaggery will come into force from April 1, 1996, railway minister Paswan said.
Producers said the hike would hurt manufacturers of commodity products such as steel, cement and plastics most.

"It would push up prices of most goods," said Anil Singhvi, treasurer at Gujarat Ambuja Cements Ltd, a leading cement maker. He said most industry officials had been expecting an 8.0-10.0 percent freight hike.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will present the centre-left coalition government's 1997/98 (April-March) budget on Friday.

Minimal market expectations from the budget include scrapping a double taxation on company dividends, allowing firms to buy back their shares. Brokers are expecting a reduction of a 7.5 percent corporate surcharge and reconfiguring a new minimum alternate tax, both of which were introduced in the last budget.
Among pivotals, Reliance rose 2.0 rupees to 263.75, SBI 0.75 to 274.75 and Tata Power 4.75 to 131.0 rupees.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
